sheets.title: Medieval Andhra: Eastern Chalukyas, Kakatiyas, Musunuris, Reddis
sheets.intro: Vengi, Kakatiya kings and tanks, Musunuri revolt, Velamas, Reddi kings and poets.

keys.name: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi

rows.v: 624; Kubja Vishnuvardhana; first seat Pishtapura (Pithapuram), then Vengi
General Pandaranga – earliest Telugu verse inscription (tarujoja metre)
c. 1019 – 1061; Rajamahendravaram; Nannaya (Adi Kavi) began Andhra Mahabharatam (2.5 parvas); Andhra Shabda Chintamani
Kulottunga I took the Chola throne 1070; Vengi merged

traps: Addanki = first Telugu verse inscription; Kalamalla = first Telugu inscription

rows.v: c. 1052 – 76; got Anumakonda (Hanamkonda) from Someshvara I
c. 1116 – 57; built power; died vs Velanati Chodas
Goddess Kakati (Durga) or Kakatipura; emblem Garuda; claimed Durjaya lineage

keys.name: Rudradeva (Prataparudra I)

rows.v: Thousand Pillar temple, Hanamkonda 1163 – star-shaped trikuta (Rudreshwara, Vishnu, Surya)
Inscriptions shift from Kannada to Telugu
Karempudi c. 1182 – Haihaya chiefs (Brahmanaidu, Nayakuralu); Palnati Viracharitra
1195 – 99; killed by Yadavas; Ganapati held by Jaitugi

traps: Palnadu war was among local chiefs

rows.v: Godavari – Krishna delta; united Telugu land
Pakhal; Laknavaram; Ramappa Cheruvu; Ganapasamudram (Ghanpur) – cascades
Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam (1244) – safety, fixed duty
Tikkana (15 parvas; Nirvachanottara Ramayanamu); Jayapa Senani – Nritta Ratnavali (1253), Gita, Vadya Ratnavali
Ramappa 1213 (general Recherla Rudra); Kota Gullu, Ghanpur
Yadavas of Devagiri; revolt of Kayastha Ambadeva
Outer earthen wall and moat at Warangal
Gona Budda Reddy – Ranganatha Ramayanam (first Telugu Ramayana)
Ulugh Khan (for Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) took Warangal → "Sultanpur"; king died near the Narmada
Malik Maqbul (convert Gannama Nayaka) governor, later Firoz's wazir
Land (nayankaramu) for keeping troops; open to any birth – later Vijayanagara
Shaiva (Kalamukha, Virashaiva); Jains tolerated; Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya
Palkuriki Somanatha – Basava Puranam, Panditaradhya Charitra; Ketana – Andhra Bhasha Bhushanamu (first Telugu grammar in Telugu); Baddena – Sumati Satakam
Kala Thoranam = Telangana emblem; Mission Kakatiya (2015)
Star-shaped platforms; polished black dolerite; floating bricks; sand-box foundation
Palampet (Mulugu); 1213; Recherla Rudra; named after sculptor; madanika brackets; UNESCO 2021 – India's 39th (Dholavira 40th)
Three walls; Swayambhu temple's four Kirti Toranas (Kala Thoranam)

keys.name: Musunuri Nayakas

rows.v: c. 1325 – 33; Rekapalle (near Bhadrachalam); Vilasa grant – laments the ruin
1333 – 68; with 75 Nayakas (Kaluvacheru grant) and Hoysala Ballala III took Warangal from Malik Maqbul 1336
Helped Hasan Gangu 1347; later lost Golconda and the Turquoise Throne to Muhammad Shah I; son Vinayaka Deva killed
Killed by Velama Anapota Nayaka at Bhimavaram 1368

traps: Turquoise Throne went to the Bahmanis

rows.v: Rasarnava Sudhakara (poetics); Potana's Bhogini Dandakam for him
Panta Reddi; were Kakatiya commanders; one of the 75 Nayakas
Cuttack / Simhachalam to Kanchi; Srisailam west; port Motupalli
c. 1325 – 1335 (or 1353); Addanki; Srisailam steps; Ahobilam temple; 108 Siva temples; title Apratima-Bhudana-Parasurama; patron of Errana
1364 – 86; customs duties abolished; Veerasiro Mandapam, Srisailam
1402 – 20; "Sarvajna Chakravarti"; Sangita Chintamani, Sahitya Chintamani; patron of Srinatha
Kataya Vema (c. 1395; Kalidasa commentary – Kumaragiriyam); queen Anitalli (Kaluvacheru grant 1423); regent Allada Reddi; Virabhadra Reddi (Srinatha's patron)

keys.name: Reddi-age poets

rows.v: Completed Aranya Parva; Nrisimha Puranamu, Harivamsamu; "Prabandha Parameswara", "Sambhudasa"

Vidyadhikari at Kondavidu; "Kavi Sarvabhauma" – kanakabhishekam by Deva Raya II (Praudha Devaraya) after beating Gauda Dindima Bhatta; Sringara Naishadhamu, Bhimakhandamu, Kasikhandamu (to Virabhadra Reddi), Haravilasamu (to Avachi Tippayya Setti), Palnati Vira Charitra
Bammera (near Warangal); Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu – to Lord Rama

traps: Praudha Devaraya = Deva Raya II, not the last Sangama

keys.name: Gajapatis and the end of the Reddis

rows.v: Kapilendra Deva 1434 (Suryavamsa); capital Kataka (Cuttack); son Hamvira took the Reddi country 1450s; Purushottama 1467 – 97; Prataparudra Deva 1497 – 1540 (Chaitanya's influence)
Krishnadevaraya took Kondavidu from Prataparudra Deva
